elements.evidence: The rendered Section 19 still binds "both parties" — i.e. Customer — with a mutual non-solicitation covering the other party's directly involved personnel for 12 months; the preferred position (no restriction on Customer at all) is not achieved.
"both parties agree not to solicit for employment any employee of the other party" — obligation runs symmetrically in both directions.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Limited to "any employee of the other party who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement"; the original catch-all reach to "any employee of the other party" (and to ex-employees within six months) has been removed.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: "for a period of twelve (12) months after a person's involvement in the provision of services under this Agreement ends" — the temporal anchor is the end of involvement, not termination, replacing the original "one year thereafter".

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: "shall not apply to general advertisements of employment not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel".

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: "or to unsolicited approaches by any such person".

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The operative verb is changed from "not to hire" to "not to solicit for employment", and an express proviso states "this Section shall not restrict either party from hiring any person"; the affiliate no-hire extension is deleted with the no-hire itself.

elements.element: The restriction is not longer than 24 months and does not cover all Vendor personnel (walk-away check).
elements.evidence: Duration is 12 months from end of involvement and scope is confined to directly involved personnel, so the clause is out of walk-away territory.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative language: mutuality, involvement-limited scope, 12-months-from-end-of-involvement duration, general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, and an express no-prohibition-on-hiring proviso all appear in the rendered clause rather than only in the margin comment.

Preferred level is correctly not claimed: Customer remains subject to a mutual non-solicit, so a "deviation" finding resolved at fallback is the right posture given the original was a mutual no-hire over all employees (walk-away).

Minimality holds: every edit maps to a selected fallback element — verb change hire→solicit for employment (no-hire element), scope narrowing (involvement element), re-anchored 12-month period (duration element), and the added proviso (carve-out and no-hire elements). Deleting "or allow its respective affiliates to hire" and the six-month former-employee tail is part of removing the no-hire and narrowing scope, not an unrelated extra; no survival tail, expense language, procedures, or boilerplate were added.

Intent is preserved: the clause remains a mutual restrictive covenant sitting in Section 19, the term-plus-tail structure survives, and no defined term, cross-reference, or retained sentence is left dangling or contradicted.

Deterministic checks (duration ≤12 months, general-solicitation carve-out present, element coverage, minimality gate) were inspected in substance against the rendered text and match; no gate is passing on a mere keyword hit.
